subject: Risk & Compliance
title: The Bank Secrecy Act
description: One-minute skill: The Bank Secrecy Act.

hook.text: In 1970, the US passed a law requiring banks to report suspicious cash. It was the birth of modern AML.

buildup.text: The Bank Secrecy Act requires banks to file Currency Transaction Reports for deposits over $10,000.

discovery.text: Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) flag unusual transactions. FinCEN receives over 4 million SARs per year.

twist.text: The vast majority of SARs lead nowhere. Banks file defensively to avoid penalties, not to catch criminals.

climax.text: BSA created the foundation for AML, but the sheer volume of reports often buries real signals in noise.

punchline.text: 4 million reports a year. Most lead nowhere. That's AML.

quiz.question: What does the Bank Secrecy Act require?
options: Banks must report suspicious transactions and large cash deposits
Banks must keep all transactions secret
Banks must refuse cash deposits over $10,000
